title: Intersections in the doubled ordinal simplex
statement: For the doubling and endpoints [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-ordinal-path], doubling sends injective simplex maps to injective maps. If q:[d] to double([a]) and t:[d] to double([b]) have equal composites under doubled injective maps e:[a] to [c], f:[b] to [c], they factor compatibly through a doubled common face. The intersection of either endpoint of [c] with double(f) is the same endpoint of [a].

source.place: Tag 017J, compatible simplex families; doubled-ordinal intersections used in hypercovering Tag 01GN

proof.text: Every doubled vertex lies uniquely in its first or second block. A doubled map preserves the block and applies the underlying map there. Therefore equal doubled images have the same block and equal underlying images. Injectivity follows blockwise.

Evaluate the compatibility equality at vertex zero to obtain a common vertex for e and f. Use the nonempty ordinal pullback and its factorization property. At every vertex the same-block observation and the ordinary pullback give range containment in the doubled first projection. Factor q through it and cancel the doubled f to identify t.

For an endpoint intersection, all vertices of t must lie in the indicated block, since the endpoint images in opposite blocks are disjoint. Factor through that endpoint by range containment and cancel the target endpoint to identify q.

lean.statement:
theorem doubled_face_intersection {a b c d : SimplexCategory}
    (e : a ⟶ c) (f : b ⟶ c) [Mono e] [Mono f]
    (q : d ⟶ obj a) (t : d ⟶ obj b) (hqt : q ≫ map e = t ≫ map f) :
    ∃ (p : SimplexCategory) (r : p ⟶ a) (s : p ⟶ b) (z : d ⟶ obj p),
      Mono r ∧ Mono s ∧ r ≫ e = s ≫ f ∧ z ≫ map r = q ∧ z ≫ map s = t
